_about: T678: the lines the coast cut (`pipeline.atlas.splits.coast`) leaves to the owner, each kept as TODAY'S atlas has it (`keep`: cut at `cut_m` / whole / fresh) until the owner decides: the two crossings disagree, the geometric crossing finds no tidal water, a slough or unnamed line on the Fraser's code, or held by name (Kitimat, item C). `at` is the line's mouth (lon, lat); `methods` what each crossing says (route measures). Written by `python -m pipeline.atlas.splits.coast_held` from a built atlas; a row with `decided` is the owner's ruling and is kept on a rerun. Read by the atlas build (`build.cut_shores`), which refuses an owner line missing here.
